messages:
sre-bot: [ALERT] Canary rollout v10 -> streaming path p99 spike in us-west-2. SLO breach: p95 ~600ms (target 250ms), p99 ~6.5s (target 1s). Affected route: /v1/stream/generate. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.io/q/streaming-canary-usw2

maya: oncall here, ack paging. starting triage.

alex: seeing corresponding spike in encoder latency on canary pods, plus KV cache miss rate up ~3x. stack: v10 (canary) -> v9 (prod).

sam: retries spiking on client side, logs show repeated 502s then streaming half-closed. sample log: `stream_sync: write failed: broken pipe` across 10 hosts.

thomas: looking at infra, GPU memory pressure increased on canary nodes during long sequences. suspect model footprint change + batching interaction.

maya: good. can we confirm traffic split? what percent on v10?

devops: traffic split = 15% -> v10. Canary autoscale looks normal, but throttles on multiplex queue increased.

alex: KV eviction events line up with p99 bumps. also see `kv_lock_waits` rising. likely contention when many long streams multiplex.

nora: CS: two enterprise customers reported stream disconnects and elevated latencies ~5m ago. they're on us-west-2. escalating to account owners.

carla: ack, I'm pinging customer success and drafting a short status note to owners.

maya: mitigation plan options: 1) reduce canary to 0% (rollback traffic), 2) scale canary nodes vertically, 3) apply temporary routing to short-circuit long-sequence multiplexing. prefer fastest: roll traffic back to v9. any objections?

sam: rollback traffic is fastest. we should also capture traces for postmortem.

thomas: +1 rollback. runbook: `redwoodctl traffic shift --from v10 --to v9 --percent 0 --reason "canary p99 spike"`

devops: executing command now. I'll annotate deploy bot. `>> redwoodctl traffic shift ...`

(systems-bot): traffic shift started: v10 15% -> 0% over 60s (initiated by devops). change id: cs-2951.

alex: while shifting, capture KV metrics and trace ids: `trace/stream/*` and `kv/locks/*`. I'll attach a short sampling script.

sam: running quick smoke: curl to stream endpoint shows initial p99 drop in progress.

thomas: infra: canary pods marked for deschedule as traffic drains. no scaling events triggered.

(systems-bot): traffic shift complete: v10 -> 0%. rollback finished in 58s. change id: cs-2951.

maya: confirm metrics: p95 back to ~240ms, p99 down to ~980ms within 2m of rollback. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.io/q/streaming-canary-usw2?until=now

nora: customers notified: CS sent preliminary note — they reported stream disconnects stopped after 3m from rollback. no data corruption reported.

carla: tagging affected accounts and next steps for an incident postmortem. will coordinate severity and communication.

alex: collected traces and KV lock histograms saved to s3: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/2951236789/traces.tgz

sam: quick root-cause hypothesis: v10 introduced a different attention kernel that increased long-sequence memory churn and KV lock contention under multiplexed streaming, exposing tail latency. needs deeper perf diff and kernel trace.

thomas: sched team to run repro with long-seq mux at 15% traffic and profiler attached. I'll open an infra ticket and assign.

maya: paging update: no further pages for now. oncall shifts to follow-up work: thomas + alex will own repro and perf diffs, sam + nora will handle customer comms. carla will draft postmortem timeline.

devops: leaving rollback markers in deploy log, will keep canary image frozen until research done.

maya: thanks everyone. leaving this thread open for the postmortem link. if anything new appears, @here. :thumbsup:

carla: postmortem stub created: https://docs.redwood.com/incidents/2951236789-canary-streaming-tail (will fill)

alex: saving final metrics snapshot and closing live mitigation. will attach perf diffs to postmortem.

maya: closing handoff — oncall clear.

(sre-bot): Incident closed: mitigation complete, SLO restored. severity: Sev2.
